title: Pause, rebuilt on the Until Dawn character-screen layout
state: mockup — nothing built, nothing in src/ touched (AGENTS.md hard rule 9)

reference.what: The Until Dawn character screen, as described to this agent in writing. No frame of the video was copied, downloaded or committed; the repo is public and hard rule 8 stands.
measuredProperties: one full-bleed cinematic close-up, head and shoulders, three-quarter, head about 75% of the frame height
no panels, boxes or cards — every line floats on the picture; huge negative space
a thin tab strip across the full width at about 6% from the top, a shoulder glyph at each end, the active tab first and brighter with a fine underline, a tiny dot beside a tab with something new

two columns of thin horizontal meter bars between 33% and 65% of the height, inside the left 48% of the width; a tiny right-aligned caps label, a hairline bar with a brighter filled segment and a small marker
bottom left at 78-84% of the height: a tiny dim caps label and one large line in a thin, widely tracked serif in caps, spanning about 45% of the width
bottom right: a single small BACK prompt with its button glyph
thin quiet typography, mostly small caps, low contrast except the active tab and the big line; slow cross-fades when the character changes

howOursDiffers: The single accent is Yevon gold (#E3B94A) in FFX chapters and pyre pink (#F7B6D9) in FFX-2 chapters, never the reference's cyan. That swap is the approved Ink & Gold rule, not an invention (presentation-ink-and-gold.md, Tokens).
The close-ups are our approved painted 2x masters from public/art/pause/, framed with CSS only. No 3D face, no new render, no edit to a pixel of an approved painting.

Type is our faces: Chakra Petch for every tracked caps label, Rajdhani for numerals, Cormorant Garamond 300 for the big line. The reference's thin grotesque is answered by Chakra Petch Medium at low opacity.

Every text is at least 14 effective CSS px at 1600x900. The reference's row pitch (about 14px at 720p) would put our labels near 12px, so the row pitch is opened to 27px and the bar is 124x3. This is a knowing departure: fix3-pause.md's whole first pass was Bailey reporting that pause chrome was unreadable.
Our objective sentences are longer than the reference's one-word labels, so the big line is allowed to wrap to a second line at 39px rather than shrink below it.
A 13% fractal-noise grain and the ink vignette from the Ink & Gold surface pass sit over the whole frame, so chrome never sits on raw paint.
Our brand line (PYREFLY REPRISE · FINAL FANTASY X) sits above the tab strip at 24% opacity. The reference has no wordmark; the current pause screen does, so it was kept rather than silently dropped.

tabs.order: the active member first (as in the reference), then the other two on the field, then CHAPTER, GUIDE, OPTIONS, CONTROLS, MUSIC
tabs.cycling: Q / E, or L1 / R1 — a glyph pair at each end of the strip
tabs.underEachMemberTab: a 2px HP hairline, red below 30%. This is where the old bottom party-card strip's at-a-glance read went.
tabs.dot: a tiny accent dot on a tab with something new — a status just landed, a track just unlocked
tabs.note: MUSIC is a sixth non-character tab, added because the jukebox has its own cursor and 21 tracks and cannot be a row. It is the one tab the brief did not name; see README question 4.

columnOne.heading: BATTLE STATS
ffx2: Agility — read off the dressphere she is wearing, at her level
columnOne.barMeaning: fill = this member's value divided by the best of the three on the field; the hairline tick = the three-member average. HP and MP fill current/max instead, and are the only rows that print a slash.
columnOne.ffx2Extension: a dimmer segment past the fill = what the Garment Grid and her two accessories add, printed as '+25' beside the number. FFX weapons and armour grant no stats at all (gagazet.ts header, research §7.7.1), so there is no such extension in an FFX chapter — that is a real difference between the games, not a missing feature.

columnTwo.heading: IN THIS FIGHT
ffx: each status, with how long it has left
Turn order — Nth of N in the CTB queue
columnTwo.statusDurationFinding: The brief asked for 'statuses with remaining duration'. In this engine's data most FFX statuses are durationModel 'battle-254' — Zombie, Haste, Slow, Shell, Protect, Reflect, Berserk, Confuse, Curse, Provoke, Poison, Petrify, Scan. They last the rest of the fight and a turn counter would be a lie. Only Silence, Sleep, Darkness and Regen are 'turns'; Doom is a 'counter'; Guard / Sentinel / Defend are 'until next turn'. So the row prints what the model actually is — REST OF BATTLE, N TURNS, or a Doom countdown. (src/data/ffx/statuses/core.ts)

bottomLeft.eyebrow: CHAPTER <n> · <location>, or the battle tally in a chained chapter (chapter 3 is four battles, chapter 5 is five)
bottomLeft.line: the chapter's current objective, verbatim from src/data/chapter-meta.ts — the first of its three that is not yet done

contentMap.bottomRight: Esc  RESUME, with a small 'H  hide panels' under it
contentMap.optionsTab: same picture, same tab strip; the rows float exactly where the meters were. Left column: master volume, music, sound effects, text speed, X-2 battle (Active/Wait), strategy guide, battle help. Right column: replay briefing, restart encounter, then a rule, then chapter select, quit to title.
contentMap.controlsTab: same picture; the rows are the key and pad map — which is where the current ControlsHint strip's chips go once the strip itself is gone.
contentMap.hidden: H still hides everything but the painting, leaving one line bottom-left: 'H show panels · Esc resume'. That is the current .pause--bare behaviour, unchanged.

gameAware.rule: AGENTS.md hard rule 14 — each element is FFX only, FFX-2 only, or both, decided from the sources.
both: the layout itself: full-bleed close-up, tab strip, two meter columns, objective line, back prompt, H to hide
column one's seven stat rows (both engines carry str/mag/def/mdef/agi on their StatBlock)
the tab strip's HP hairline and 'something new' dot
OPTIONS, CONTROLS, CHAPTER, GUIDE, MUSIC as tabs
the grade, the grain and the vignette
ffxOnly: column two's Overdrive gauge and Overdrive mode
Turn order — 'Nth of N' is CTB; ATB has no queue to be Nth in
status rows that read REST OF BATTLE (the battle-254 model is FFX's)
ffx2Only: pink as the accent (presentation-ink-and-gold.md: --pyre-pink replaces gold for the whole accent role in FFX-2 chapters)
column two's ATB gauge, Active/Wait mode, Chain, Dressphere, Garment Grid and gate count
the dim bar extension for grid and accessory bonuses
column one reading off the worn dressphere rather than a fixed character stat block

dataSources.ffxStats: src/data/ffx/builds/gagazet.ts (research/ffx-seymour-flux.md §7.3) — Tidus 2420/115, 31/16/20/18/30; Yuna 1500/270, 15/37/13/39/15; Kimahri 2310/130, 26/22/22/16/18. Overdrive gauges and modes from the same file (Tidus warrior, Yuna healer).
dataSources.ffx2Stats: the dressphere x level tables each girl is wearing at the chapter 4 build point — gunner.ts L23 (970/56, 49/26/31/31/53), dark-knight.ts L24, warrior.ts L25; bonuses from bevelle.ts accessories (circlet Mag+10/MDef+10, mythril gloves Def+20) and garment-grids/early.ts protection-halo (Def+5/MDef+5, 4 gate colours).
dataSources.invented: Only the live battle state a paused screen would happen to be showing — current HP/MP/gauge values, which statuses are up, the turn position, the chain count. No stat, cap, duration or name is invented.
